scope: Exodus 28–31, all 145 public verses. Prior revisions remain unchanged.

source.verse_hash_method: SHA-256 of the exact original XML verse substring, including written/read notes, not a normalized substitute.
source.public_versification_note: Public and Hebrew numbering align throughout Exodus 28–31.

delta_method: F0 retained wording; F1 lexical; F2 syntax/idiom; F3 consequential interpretive, textual, social, or versification choice. Editorial assessments are separate from similarity scores. Independent review has not occurred.

verses.rationale: Keeps brother relationship, selection from Israel, priestly purpose and all five names rather than an anonymous priesthood.
verses.before: “And you, bring near to yourself Aaron your brother and his sons with him from among the children of Israel, to serve as priests to me: Aaron, Nadab and Abihu, Eleazar and Ithamar, Aaron’s sons.
verses.after: “Bring your brother Aaron and his sons near to you from among the Israelites, so they may serve me as priests: Aaron and his sons Nadab, Abihu, Eleazar, and Ithamar.
verses.tsw_comparator: “And you, bring near to yourself Aaron your brother and his sons with him from among the children of Israel, to serve as priests to me: Aaron, Nadab and Abihu, Eleazar and Ithamar, Aaron’s sons.

verses.rationale: Retains holiness and both purposes, including beauty explicitly present in the source.
verses.before: You will make holy garments for Aaron your brother, for glory and for beauty.
verses.after: Make holy garments for your brother Aaron, for honor and beauty.
verses.tsw_comparator: You shall make holy garments for Aaron your brother, for glory and for beauty.

verses.rationale: Renders wise-hearted as practical skill while retaining divine filling and spirit of wisdom, not reducing it to unaided craftsmanship.
verses.before: You will speak to all the wise of heart, whom I have filled with a spirit of skill, that they make Aaron’s garments to consecrate him, so that he may serve as priest to me.
verses.after: Speak to all the skilled workers whom I have filled with a spirit of wisdom. Have them make Aaron’s garments to consecrate him for service to me as a priest.
verses.tsw_comparator: You shall speak to all the wise of heart, whom I have filled with a spirit of skill, that they make Aaron’s garments to consecrate him, so that he may serve as priest to me.

verses.rationale: Keeps six garment categories and repeated purpose; patterned leaves precise tashbets textile technique open.
verses.before: These are the garments that they will make: a breastpiece, an ephod, a robe, a woven tunic, a turban, and a sash. They will make holy garments for Aaron your brother and for his sons, so that he may serve as priest to me.
verses.after: These are the garments they are to make: a breastpiece, an ephod, a robe, a patterned tunic, a turban, and a sash. They are to make holy garments for your brother Aaron and his sons, so they may serve me as priests.
verses.tsw_comparator: These are the garments that they shall make: a breastpiece, an ephod, a robe, a woven tunic, a turban, and a sash. They shall make holy garments for Aaron your brother and for his sons, so that he may serve as priest to me.

verses.rationale: Preserves material list and skilled workers as agents; yarn supplied from textile context.
verses.before: They will take the gold, the blue, the purple, the scarlet yarn, and the fine linen.
verses.after: They are to use gold, blue, purple, and scarlet yarn, and fine linen.
verses.tsw_comparator: They shall take the gold, the blue, the purple, the scarlet yarn, and the fine linen.

verses.rationale: Keeps ephod name, skilled design, gold and all fabric specifications.
verses.before: “They will make the ephod of gold, blue, purple, and scarlet yarn, and fine twisted linen, the work of a skilled designer.
verses.after: Have them make the ephod with a skilled design, using gold, blue, purple, and scarlet yarn, and finely twisted linen.
verses.tsw_comparator: “They shall make the ephod of gold, blue, purple, and scarlet yarn, and fine twisted linen, the work of a skilled designer.

verses.rationale: Preserves two pieces and two-end connection without claiming a complete garment reconstruction.
verses.before: It will have two shoulder pieces joined to its two edges, so that it is joined together.
verses.after: It is to have two shoulder pieces joined at its two ends to hold it together.
verses.tsw_comparator: It shall have two shoulder pieces joined to its two edges, so that it is joined together.

verses.rationale: Keeps integral waistband and repeats all materials rather than referring back by shorthand.
verses.before: The skillfully woven band that is on it, with which it is fastened, will be of one piece and like its workmanship: of gold, blue, purple, and scarlet yarn, and fine twisted linen.
verses.after: Its woven waistband must be of one piece with it and made the same way: gold, blue, purple, and scarlet yarn, and finely twisted linen.
verses.tsw_comparator: The skillfully woven band that is on it, with which it is fastened, shall be of one piece and like its workmanship: of gold, blue, purple, and scarlet yarn, and fine twisted linen.

verses.rationale: Retains two stones and Israel’s sons as names, with command continuing into their distribution.
verses.before: You will take two onyx stones and engrave on them the names of the children of Israel,
verses.after: Take two onyx stones and engrave on them the names of Israel’s sons,
verses.tsw_comparator: You shall take two onyx stones and engrave on them the names of the children of Israel,

verses.rationale: Keeps six plus six and birth order rather than substituting an unstated tribal arrangement.
verses.before: six of their names on one stone and the names of the remaining six on the other stone, according to their birth.
verses.after: six names on one stone and the six remaining names on the other, in their birth order.
verses.tsw_comparator: six of their names on one stone and the names of the remaining six on the other stone, according to their birth.

verses.rationale: Preserves signet engraving comparison, names and encasing gold.
verses.before: As the work of a stone engraver, like the engraving of a signet, you will engrave the two stones with the names of the children of Israel. You will set them in settings of gold.
verses.after: Engrave the two stones with the names of Israel’s sons as a stoneworker engraves a seal. Set them in gold settings.
verses.tsw_comparator: As the work of a stone engraver, like the engraving of a signet, you shall engrave the two stones with the names of the children of Israel. You shall set them in settings of gold.

verses.rationale: Retains doubled memorial language and bodily name-bearing on two shoulders.
verses.before: You will put the two stones on the shoulder pieces of the ephod as stones of remembrance for the children of Israel. Aaron will bear their names before the LORD on his two shoulders for remembrance.
verses.after: Place the two stones on the ephod’s shoulder pieces as memorial stones for Israel’s sons. Aaron will carry their names on his two shoulders before the LORD as a memorial.
verses.tsw_comparator: You shall put the two stones on the shoulder pieces of the ephod as stones of remembrance for the children of Israel. Aaron shall bear their names before the LORD on his two shoulders for remembrance.

verses.rationale: Keeps brief setting instruction as sentence continued into chains.
verses.before: You will make settings of gold
verses.after: Make gold settings,
verses.tsw_comparator: You shall make settings of gold

verses.rationale: Chooses twisted cord construction for compact chain terms without specifying an uncertain measured length.
verses.before: and two chains of pure gold, twisted like cords, and attach the corded chains to the settings.
verses.after: and two chains of pure gold, twisted like cords, and attach the corded chains to the settings.
verses.tsw_comparator: and two chains of pure gold, twisted like cords, and attach the corded chains to the settings.

verses.rationale: Keeps mishpat as judgment connected to rulings and later Urim/Thummim, not merely decorative jewelry.
verses.before: “You will make a breastpiece of judgment, the work of a skilled designer. Like the workmanship of the ephod you will make it: of gold, blue, purple, and scarlet yarn, and fine twisted linen.
verses.after: Make a breastpiece for judgment with a skilled design, made like the ephod: gold, blue, purple, and scarlet yarn, and finely twisted linen.
verses.tsw_comparator: “You shall make a breastpiece of judgment, the work of a skilled designer. Like the workmanship of the ephod you shall make it: of gold, blue, purple, and scarlet yarn, and fine twisted linen.

verses.rationale: Preserves doubled construction, square shape and two span dimensions in ancient units.
verses.before: It will be square and folded double, a span long and a span wide.
verses.after: It must be square when folded double, a span long and a span wide.
verses.tsw_comparator: It shall be square and folded double, a span long and a span wide.

verses.rationale: Keeps first three Hebrew stone positions with provisional traditional mineral equivalents; exact identifications noted as uncertain.
verses.before: You will set in it settings of stones, four rows of stones. A row of carnelian, topaz, and emerald will be the first row;
verses.after: Set four rows of stones in it. The first row is to be carnelian, topaz, and emerald;
verses.tsw_comparator: You shall set in it settings of stones, four rows of stones. A row of carnelian, topaz, and emerald shall be the first row;

verses.rationale: Preserves nofekh-sappir-yahalom order with provisional names; sapphire matches the earlier 24:10 terminology.
verses.before: the second row: turquoise, sapphire, and diamond;
verses.after: the second row, turquoise, sapphire, and moonstone;
verses.tsw_comparator: the second row: turquoise, sapphire, and diamond;

verses.rationale: Keeps leshem-shevo-ahlama positions without pretending modern mineral equivalents are established.
verses.before: the third row: jacinth, agate, and amethyst;
verses.after: the third row, jacinth, agate, and amethyst;
verses.tsw_comparator: the third row: jacinth, agate, and amethyst;

verses.rationale: Keeps final three stones, shoham consistent with shoulder stones and all gold settings; names remain provisional.
verses.before: the fourth row: beryl, onyx, and jasper. They will be enclosed in gold settings.
verses.after: and the fourth row, beryl, onyx, and jasper. Mount them in gold settings.
verses.tsw_comparator: the fourth row: beryl, onyx, and jasper. They shall be enclosed in gold settings.

verses.rationale: Keeps twelve stones, individual names, signet comparison and explicit connection of sons to tribes.
verses.before: The stones will be according to the names of the children of Israel, twelve according to their names. Like the engravings of a signet, each will be according to its name, for the twelve tribes.
verses.after: There must be twelve stones bearing the names of Israel’s sons. Engrave each with one name, like a seal, for the twelve tribes.
verses.tsw_comparator: The stones shall be according to the names of the children of Israel, twelve according to their names. Like the engravings of a signet, each shall be according to its name, for the twelve tribes.

verses.rationale: Retains repeated chain construction specifically for breastpiece without assuming new measured dimensions.
verses.before: “You will make for the breastpiece twisted chains like cords, of pure gold.
verses.after: Make chains of pure gold for the breastpiece, twisted like cords.
verses.tsw_comparator: “You shall make for the breastpiece twisted chains like cords, of pure gold.

verses.rationale: Keeps pair count, gold and two-end placement.
verses.before: You will make for the breastpiece two rings of gold and put the two rings on the two ends of the breastpiece.
verses.after: Make two gold rings for the breastpiece and attach them to its two ends.
verses.tsw_comparator: You shall make for the breastpiece two rings of gold and put the two rings on the two ends of the breastpiece.

verses.rationale: Preserves two cords and two rings with explicit fastening relationship.
verses.before: You will put the two cords of gold into the two rings at the ends of the breastpiece.
verses.after: Attach the two gold cords to the two rings at the ends of the breastpiece.
verses.tsw_comparator: You shall put the two cords of gold into the two rings at the ends of the breastpiece.

verses.rationale: Clarifies free ends attaching to shoulder settings and front orientation without deleting repeated two.
verses.before: You will put the two ends of the two cords on the two settings and attach them to the shoulder pieces of the ephod at its front.
verses.after: Attach the other ends of the two cords to the two settings, fastening them to the shoulder pieces on the front of the ephod.
verses.tsw_comparator: You shall put the two ends of the two cords on the two settings and attach them to the shoulder pieces of the ephod at its front.

verses.rationale: Distinguishes additional rings from the first pair and keeps inward-facing edge.
verses.before: You will make two rings of gold and put them on the two ends of the breastpiece, on its inner edge next to the ephod.
verses.after: Make two more gold rings and put them at the two ends of the breastpiece, on its inner edge facing the ephod.
verses.tsw_comparator: You shall make two rings of gold and put them on the two ends of the breastpiece, on its inner edge next to the ephod.

verses.rationale: Keeps lower/front location, seam relation and above-waistband distinction in readable sequence.
verses.before: You will make two more rings of gold and put them on the two shoulder pieces of the ephod, low on its front, near its joining, above the woven band of the ephod.
verses.after: Make two gold rings and attach them low on the front of the ephod’s two shoulder pieces, near the seam and above its waistband.
verses.tsw_comparator: You shall make two more rings of gold and put them on the two shoulder pieces of the ephod, low on its front, near its joining, above the woven band of the ephod.

verses.rationale: Preserves blue tie, waistband relation and prevention of movement; retains plural rings, with the written/read spelling annotation bound in full.
verses.before: They will bind the breastpiece by its rings to the rings of the ephod with a cord of blue yarn, so that it rests on the woven band of the ephod and the breastpiece does not come loose from the ephod.
verses.after: Tie the breastpiece’s rings to the ephod’s rings with a blue cord, so the breastpiece sits above the waistband and does not come loose from the ephod.
verses.tsw_comparator: They shall bind the breastpiece by its rings to the rings of the ephod with a cord of blue yarn, so that it rests on the woven band of the ephod and the breastpiece does not come loose from the ephod.

verses.rationale: Keeps recurring name-bearing now on heart, sanctuary entry and continuous memorial purpose.
verses.before: So Aaron will bear the names of the children of Israel in the breastpiece of judgment over his heart when he enters the Holy Place, as a continual remembrance before the LORD.
verses.after: Whenever Aaron enters the sanctuary, he will carry the names of Israel’s sons over his heart on the breastpiece for judgment, as a continual memorial before the LORD.
verses.tsw_comparator: So Aaron shall bear the names of the children of Israel in the breastpiece of judgment over his heart when he enters the Holy Place, as a continual remembrance before the LORD.

verses.rationale: Retains named objects and repeated judgment/heart language; notes their unresolved form and procedure without inventing a divination mechanism.
verses.before: You will put the Urim and the Thummim into the breastpiece of judgment, and they will be over Aaron’s heart when he enters before the LORD. Aaron will bear the judgment of the children of Israel over his heart before the LORD continually.
verses.after: Place the Urim and Thummim in the breastpiece for judgment, so they will be over Aaron’s heart when he enters before the LORD. Aaron will continually carry Israel’s judgment over his heart before the LORD.
verses.tsw_comparator: You shall put the Urim and the Thummim into the breastpiece of judgment, and they shall be over Aaron’s heart when he enters before the LORD. Aaron shall bear the judgment of the children of Israel over his heart before the LORD continually.

verses.rationale: Keeps wholly blue robe distinct from multicolor ephod and clarifies relationship without specifying unstated layering.
verses.before: “You will make the robe of the ephod entirely of blue.
verses.after: Make the robe worn with the ephod entirely of blue fabric.
verses.tsw_comparator: “You shall make the robe of the ephod entirely of blue.

verses.rationale: Preserves head opening, woven reinforcement, armor comparison and no-tearing purpose; rare tahra identification qualified in note.
verses.before: There will be an opening for his head in its middle. Around its opening will be a woven binding, like the opening of a coat of armor, so that it does not tear.
verses.after: It is to have an opening for the head in the middle, with a woven edge all around it, like the opening of a coat of armor, so it will not tear.
verses.tsw_comparator: There shall be an opening for his head in its middle. Around its opening shall be a woven binding, like the opening of a coat of armor, so that it does not tear.

verses.rationale: Keeps three colors, fruit forms, gold bells and circumferential placement.
verses.before: On its hem you will make pomegranates of blue, purple, and scarlet yarn around its hem, with bells of gold between them all around:
verses.after: Around its hem, make pomegranates of blue, purple, and scarlet yarn, with gold bells between them all the way around.
verses.tsw_comparator: On its hem you shall make pomegranates of blue, purple, and scarlet yarn around its hem, with bells of gold between them all around:

verses.rationale: Preserves patterned repetition rather than replacing it with a summary of alternating ornaments.
verses.before: a gold bell and a pomegranate, a gold bell and a pomegranate, around the hem of the robe.
verses.after: A gold bell and a pomegranate, a gold bell and a pomegranate, all around the robe’s hem.
verses.tsw_comparator: a gold bell and a pomegranate, a gold bell and a pomegranate, around the hem of the robe.

verses.rationale: Keeps audible entry and exit requirement and real death warning rather than ornamental symbolism.
verses.before: It will be on Aaron when he ministers, and its sound will be heard when he enters the Holy Place before the LORD and when he comes out, so that he does not die.
verses.after: Aaron must wear it while serving. Its sound must be heard when he enters the sanctuary before the LORD and when he leaves, so he will not die.
verses.tsw_comparator: It shall be on Aaron when he ministers, and its sound shall be heard when he enters the Holy Place before the LORD and when he comes out, so that he does not die.

verses.rationale: Retains plate material, signet comparison and exact short consecration inscription.
verses.before: “You will make a plate of pure gold and engrave on it, like the engraving of a signet: ‘Holy to the LORD.’
verses.after: Make a plate of pure gold and engrave on it, like a seal: ‘Holy to the LORD.’
verses.tsw_comparator: “You shall make a plate of pure gold and engrave on it, like the engraving of a signet: ‘Holy to the LORD.’

verses.rationale: Combines repeated turban reference while preserving blue attachment and front position.
verses.before: You will put it on a cord of blue yarn, and it will be on the turban; it will be on the front of the turban.
verses.after: Fasten it with a blue cord on the front of the turban.
verses.tsw_comparator: You shall put it on a cord of blue yarn, and it shall be on the turban; it shall be on the front of the turban.

verses.rationale: Preserves bearing guilt of sacred gifts and acceptance purpose without substituting personal sinlessness or moralizing priestly responsibility.
verses.before: It will be on Aaron’s forehead, and Aaron will bear the guilt connected with the holy things that the children of Israel consecrate, all their holy gifts. It will be on his forehead continually, so that they may be accepted before the LORD.
verses.after: It is to rest on Aaron’s forehead. Aaron will bear the guilt associated with the holy gifts the Israelites consecrate, whatever their holy gifts may be. It must remain on his forehead continually, so they may be accepted before the LORD.
verses.tsw_comparator: It shall be on Aaron’s forehead, and Aaron shall bear the guilt connected with the holy things that the children of Israel consecrate, all their holy gifts. It shall be on his forehead continually, so that they may be accepted before the LORD.

verses.rationale: Keeps three garment tasks and distinguishes patterned weaving from embroidered sash while leaving exact weave uncertain.
verses.before: You will weave the tunic of fine linen, make a turban of fine linen, and make a sash, the work of an embroiderer.
verses.after: Weave the tunic in a pattern of fine linen, make a fine linen turban, and make a sash worked in embroidery.
verses.tsw_comparator: You shall weave the tunic of fine linen, make a turban of fine linen, and make a sash, the work of an embroiderer.

verses.rationale: Preserves sons’ three garment categories and repeats honor/beauty from Aaron’s garments.
verses.before: “For Aaron’s sons you will make tunics, and you will make sashes for them, and you will make head coverings for them, for glory and for beauty.
verses.after: For Aaron’s sons, make tunics, sashes, and head coverings, for honor and beauty.
verses.tsw_comparator: “For Aaron’s sons you shall make tunics, and you shall make sashes for them, and you shall make head coverings for them, for glory and for beauty.

verses.rationale: Unfolds actions distinctly and translates fill-the-hand idiom as ordain with literal wording explained for later ritual connection.
verses.before: You will put these on Aaron your brother and on his sons with him. You will anoint them, fill their hands, and consecrate them, so that they may serve as priests to me.
verses.after: Dress your brother Aaron and his sons in these garments. Anoint them, ordain them, and consecrate them to serve me as priests.
verses.tsw_comparator: You shall put these on Aaron your brother and on his sons with him. You shall anoint them, fill their hands, and consecrate them, so that they may serve as priests to me.

verses.rationale: Keeps nakedness, linen and exact bodily coverage rather than euphemizing the requirement.
verses.before: You will make linen undergarments for them to cover naked flesh; they will reach from the waist to the thighs.
verses.after: Make linen undergarments for them to cover their naked flesh, reaching from the waist to the thighs.
verses.tsw_comparator: You shall make linen undergarments for them to cover naked flesh; they shall reach from the waist to the thighs.

verses.rationale: Keeps both service contexts, guilt and death, hereditary obligation and explicitly male priestly participants.
verses.before: They will be on Aaron and on his sons when they enter the tent of meeting or when they approach the altar to minister in the Holy Place, so that they do not bear guilt and die. It will be a perpetual statute for him and for his offspring after him.
verses.after: Aaron and his sons must wear them when entering the tent of meeting or approaching the altar to serve in the sanctuary, so they do not incur guilt and die. This is a lasting ordinance for Aaron and his descendants after him.”
verses.tsw_comparator: They shall be on Aaron and on his sons when they enter the tent of meeting or when they approach the altar to minister in the Holy Place, so that they do not bear guilt and die. It shall be a perpetual statute for him and for his offspring after him.

verses.rationale: Preserves consecration purpose and exact animal numbers, age category and soundness requirement.
verses.before: “And this is what you will do to them to consecrate them, so that they may serve as priests to me: take one young bull and two rams without blemish,
verses.after: “This is what you are to do to consecrate them to serve me as priests. Take one young bull and two rams without blemish,
verses.tsw_comparator: “And this is what you shall do to them to consecrate them, so that they may serve as priests to me: take one young bull and two rams without blemish,

verses.rationale: Keeps three unleavened forms, mixed versus applied oil, and wheat flour rather than collapsing all bread into one loaf.
verses.before: unleavened bread, unleavened cakes mixed with oil, and unleavened wafers spread with oil. You will make them of fine wheat flour.
verses.after: along with unleavened bread, unleavened cakes mixed with oil, and unleavened wafers brushed with oil. Make them from fine wheat flour.
verses.tsw_comparator: unleavened bread, unleavened cakes mixed with oil, and unleavened wafers spread with oil. You shall make them of fine wheat flour.

verses.rationale: Preserves one basket and repeated basket presentation with all three animals.
verses.before: You will put them in one basket and bring them in the basket, along with the bull and the two rams.
verses.after: Put them in one basket and bring them in the basket, together with the bull and the two rams.
verses.tsw_comparator: You shall put them in one basket and bring them in the basket, along with the bull and the two rams.

verses.rationale: Keeps Moses as washing agent, all priestly recipients and entry location.
verses.before: You will bring Aaron and his sons to the entrance of the tent of meeting and wash them with water.
verses.after: Bring Aaron and his sons to the entrance of the tent of meeting and wash them with water.
verses.tsw_comparator: You shall bring Aaron and his sons to the entrance of the tent of meeting and wash them with water.

verses.rationale: Preserves dressing sequence and specific waistband fastening.
verses.before: Then you will take the garments and clothe Aaron with the tunic, the robe of the ephod, the ephod, and the breastpiece, and bind the ephod upon him with its woven band.
verses.after: Take the garments and dress Aaron in the tunic, the robe worn with the ephod, the ephod, and the breastpiece. Fasten the ephod on him with its waistband.
verses.tsw_comparator: Then you shall take the garments and clothe Aaron with the tunic, the robe of the ephod, the ephod, and the breastpiece, and bind the ephod upon him with its woven band.

verses.rationale: Keeps turban/head and sacred diadem relationship, connecting to plate in note rather than replacing source title.
verses.before: You will set the turban on his head and put the holy crown upon the turban.
verses.after: Place the turban on his head and put the holy diadem on the turban.
verses.tsw_comparator: You shall set the turban on his head and put the holy crown upon the turban.

verses.rationale: Retains pouring and anointing as separate stated actions with head location.
verses.before: You will take the anointing oil, pour it on his head, and anoint him.
verses.after: Take the anointing oil, pour it on his head, and anoint him.
verses.tsw_comparator: You shall take the anointing oil, pour it on his head, and anoint him.

verses.rationale: Keeps sons distinct from Aaron and their tunic dressing.
verses.before: Then you will bring his sons and clothe them with tunics.
verses.after: Bring his sons forward and dress them in tunics.
verses.tsw_comparator: Then you shall bring his sons and clothe them with tunics.

verses.rationale: Preserves inclusive Aaron-and-sons sash clause, head coverings, permanent priesthood and repeated fill-hands idiom.
verses.before: You will gird them with sashes, Aaron and his sons, and bind head coverings on them. The priesthood will be theirs by a perpetual statute. Thus you will fill the hands of Aaron and his sons.
verses.after: Tie sashes on Aaron and his sons, and put the head coverings on them. The priesthood will be theirs by a lasting ordinance. In this way ordain Aaron and his sons.
verses.tsw_comparator: You shall gird them with sashes, Aaron and his sons, and bind head coverings on them. The priesthood shall be theirs by a perpetual statute. Thus you shall fill the hands of Aaron and his sons.

verses.rationale: Keeps presentation and hand placement without adding an unstated explanation of transferred sin.
verses.before: “You will bring the bull before the tent of meeting, and Aaron and his sons will lay their hands on the head of the bull.
verses.after: Bring the bull before the tent of meeting. Aaron and his sons are to lay their hands on its head.
verses.tsw_comparator: “You shall bring the bull before the tent of meeting, and Aaron and his sons shall lay their hands on the head of the bull.

verses.rationale: Names slaughter plainly, preserving Moses’ action and precise divine/physical setting.
verses.before: You will slaughter the bull before the LORD at the entrance of the tent of meeting.
verses.after: Slaughter the bull before the LORD at the entrance of the tent of meeting.
verses.tsw_comparator: You shall slaughter the bull before the LORD at the entrance of the tent of meeting.

verses.rationale: Keeps finger application to horns distinct from pouring remainder at base; remaining resolves prior partial use.
verses.before: You will take some of the blood of the bull and put it on the horns of the altar with your finger, and pour all the rest of the blood at the base of the altar.
verses.after: With your finger, put some of the bull’s blood on the altar’s horns. Pour all the remaining blood at the base of the altar.
verses.tsw_comparator: You shall take some of the blood of the bull and put it on the horns of the altar with your finger, and pour all the rest of the blood at the base of the altar.

verses.rationale: Preserves organ/fat list and smoke-offering verb; liver appendage rendered lobe with anatomical uncertainty noted.
verses.before: You will take all the fat that covers the entrails, the appendage of the liver, and the two kidneys with the fat that is on them, and burn them on the altar.
verses.after: Take all the fat covering the inner organs, the lobe attached to the liver, and both kidneys with their fat, and burn them on the altar as smoke.
verses.tsw_comparator: You shall take all the fat that covers the entrails, the appendage of the liver, and the two kidneys with the fat that is on them, and burn them on the altar.

verses.rationale: Keeps three discarded components, outside location and sin-offering category, distinguishing disposal burning from altar smoke.
verses.before: But the flesh of the bull, its skin, and its dung you will burn with fire outside the camp. It is a sin offering.
verses.after: Burn the bull’s meat, hide, and dung outside the camp. It is a sin offering.
verses.tsw_comparator: But the flesh of the bull, its skin, and its dung you shall burn with fire outside the camp. It is a sin offering.

verses.rationale: Retains first ram and repeated laying-on-hands action without shorthand.
verses.before: “Then you will take one ram, and Aaron and his sons will lay their hands on the head of the ram.
verses.after: Take one ram, and have Aaron and his sons lay their hands on its head.
verses.tsw_comparator: “Then you shall take one ram, and Aaron and his sons shall lay their hands on the head of the ram.

verses.rationale: Preserves slaughter, blood collection and surrounding altar application with zaraq matching chapter 24.
verses.before: You will slaughter the ram, take its blood, and throw it against the altar on all sides.
verses.after: Slaughter the ram, take its blood, and splash it against every side of the altar.
verses.tsw_comparator: You shall slaughter the ram, take its blood, and throw it against the altar on all sides.

verses.rationale: Keeps dismemberment, washing and all body categories without gratuitous elaboration or erasure.
verses.before: You will cut the ram into its pieces, wash its entrails and legs, and put them with its pieces and its head.
verses.after: Cut the ram into pieces. Wash its inner organs and legs, and place them with the pieces and the head.
verses.tsw_comparator: You shall cut the ram into its pieces, wash its entrails and legs, and put them with its pieces and its head.

verses.rationale: Retains complete ram, offering category, sensory aroma and repeated divine recipient.
verses.before: You will burn the whole ram on the altar. It is a burnt offering to the LORD, a pleasing aroma, an offering by fire to the LORD.
verses.after: Burn the whole ram on the altar as smoke. It is a burnt offering to the LORD, a pleasing aroma, an offering by fire to the LORD.
verses.tsw_comparator: You shall burn the whole ram on the altar. It is a burnt offering to the LORD, a pleasing aroma, an offering by fire to the LORD.

verses.rationale: Keeps second ram distinction and full repeated hand-laying.
verses.before: “Then you will take the second ram, and Aaron and his sons will lay their hands on the head of the ram.
verses.after: Take the second ram, and have Aaron and his sons lay their hands on its head.
verses.tsw_comparator: “Then you shall take the second ram, and Aaron and his sons shall lay their hands on the head of the ram.

verses.rationale: Preserves precise right-sided ear/hand/foot application for all named priests and remaining altar action; does not invent symbolism.
verses.before: You will slaughter the ram, take some of its blood, and put it on the lobe of Aaron’s right ear, on the lobes of his sons’ right ears, on the thumbs of their right hands, and on the big toes of their right feet. Then throw the rest of the blood against the altar on all sides.
verses.after: Slaughter the ram. Put some of its blood on the right earlobes of Aaron and his sons, on their right thumbs, and on their right big toes. Splash the blood against every side of the altar.
verses.tsw_comparator: You shall slaughter the ram, take some of its blood, and put it on the lobe of Aaron’s right ear, on the lobes of his sons’ right ears, on the thumbs of their right hands, and on the big toes of their right feet. Then throw the rest of the blood against the altar on all sides.

verses.rationale: Preserves source of blood and oil and repeated persons/garments list, distinguishing sprinkle from splash.
verses.before: You will take some of the blood that is on the altar and some of the anointing oil and sprinkle it on Aaron and his garments, and on his sons and the garments of his sons with him. Then he and his garments will be holy, and his sons and their garments with him.
verses.after: Take some blood from the altar and some anointing oil, and sprinkle them on Aaron and his garments, and on his sons and their garments. Then he and his garments, and his sons and their garments, will be consecrated.
verses.tsw_comparator: You shall take some of the blood that is on the altar and some of the anointing oil and sprinkle it on Aaron and his garments, and on his sons and the garments of his sons with him. Then he and his garments shall be holy, and his sons and their garments with him.

verses.rationale: Keeps full list including fat tail and right thigh, with ordination rationale retained.
verses.before: “You will take from the ram the fat, the fat tail, the fat that covers the entrails, the appendage of the liver, the two kidneys with the fat that is on them, and the right thigh, for it is a ram of ordination,
verses.after: Take from the ram its fat, its fat tail, the fat covering the inner organs, the lobe of the liver, both kidneys with their fat, and the right thigh, because this is the ram of ordination.
verses.tsw_comparator: “You shall take from the ram the fat, the fat tail, the fat that covers the entrails, the appendage of the liver, the two kidneys with the fat that is on them, and the right thigh, for it is a ram of ordination,

verses.rationale: Keeps one each of three breads and basket’s location before the LORD.
verses.before: and one loaf of bread, one cake of bread with oil, and one wafer from the basket of unleavened bread that is before the LORD.
verses.after: From the basket of unleavened bread before the LORD, take one round loaf, one cake made with oil, and one wafer.
verses.tsw_comparator: and one loaf of bread, one cake of bread with oil, and one wafer from the basket of unleavened bread that is before the LORD.

verses.rationale: Retains literal hands filled by portions and tenufah presentation, with uncertainty about exact motion noted.
verses.before: You will put all these in the palms of Aaron and in the palms of his sons, and wave them as a wave offering before the LORD.
verses.after: Put all of these on the palms of Aaron and his sons, and wave them as a wave offering before the LORD.
verses.tsw_comparator: You shall put all these in the palms of Aaron and in the palms of his sons, and wave them as a wave offering before the LORD.

verses.rationale: Preserves removal, layered altar offering, sensory phrase and repeated recipient.
verses.before: Then you will take them from their hands and burn them on the altar with the burnt offering as a pleasing aroma before the LORD. It is an offering by fire to the LORD.
verses.after: Take them from their hands and burn them on the altar over the burnt offering, as a pleasing aroma before the LORD. It is an offering by fire to the LORD.
verses.tsw_comparator: Then you shall take them from their hands and burn them on the altar with the burnt offering as a pleasing aroma before the LORD. It is an offering by fire to the LORD.

verses.rationale: Keeps breast specifically allotted to addressed Moses, not automatically to Aaron.
verses.before: You will take the breast from the ram of Aaron’s ordination and wave it as a wave offering before the LORD, and it will be your portion.
verses.after: Take the breast of the ram used for Aaron’s ordination and wave it as a wave offering before the LORD. It will be your portion.
verses.tsw_comparator: You shall take the breast from the ram of Aaron’s ordination and wave it as a wave offering before the LORD, and it shall be your portion.

verses.rationale: Keeps breast/waving and thigh/contribution distinction without collapsing the two technical terms.
verses.before: You will consecrate the breast of the wave offering and the thigh of the contribution that was waved and lifted up from the ram of ordination, from what belongs to Aaron and his sons.
verses.after: Consecrate the breast that was waved and the thigh that was contributed, the portions presented from the ordination ram for Aaron and his sons.
verses.tsw_comparator: You shall consecrate the breast of the wave offering and the thigh of the contribution that was waved and lifted up from the ram of ordination, from that which belongs to Aaron and his sons.

verses.rationale: Preserves enduring priestly allocation, repeated contribution and peace offerings consistent with prior chapters.
verses.before: It will belong to Aaron and his sons as a perpetual portion from the children of Israel, for it is a contribution. It will be a contribution from the children of Israel from their offerings of well-being, their contribution to the LORD.
verses.after: These will belong to Aaron and his sons as a lasting share from the Israelites. It is a contribution, to be given by the Israelites from their peace offerings as their contribution to the LORD.
verses.tsw_comparator: It shall belong to Aaron and his sons as a perpetual portion from the children of Israel, for it is a contribution. It shall be a contribution from the children of Israel from their offerings of well-being, their contribution to the LORD.

verses.rationale: Keeps garments’ succession and both installation actions rather than general inherited office alone.
verses.before: “The holy garments of Aaron will belong to his sons after him, to be anointed in them and to have their hands filled in them.
verses.after: Aaron’s holy garments are to pass to his sons after him, to be worn when they are anointed and ordained.
verses.tsw_comparator: “The holy garments of Aaron shall belong to his sons after him, to be anointed in them and to have their hands filled in them.

verses.rationale: Preserves singular successor from sons, seven-day wearing and sanctuary ministry.
verses.before: Seven days the son who becomes priest in his place will wear them when he enters the tent of meeting to minister in the Holy Place.
verses.after: The son who succeeds him as priest and enters the tent of meeting to serve in the sanctuary must wear them for seven days.
verses.tsw_comparator: Seven days the son who becomes priest in his place shall wear them when he enters the tent of meeting to minister in the Holy Place.

verses.rationale: Retains cooking, meat and holy location without importing a later kitchen arrangement.
verses.before: “You will take the ram of ordination and boil its flesh in a holy place.
verses.after: Take the ram of ordination and boil its meat in a holy place.
verses.tsw_comparator: “You shall take the ram of ordination and boil its flesh in a holy place.

verses.rationale: Keeps named diners, two food groups and precise dining location.
verses.before: Aaron and his sons will eat the flesh of the ram and the bread that is in the basket at the entrance of the tent of meeting.
verses.after: Aaron and his sons are to eat the ram’s meat and the bread in the basket at the entrance of the tent of meeting.
verses.tsw_comparator: Aaron and his sons shall eat the flesh of the ram and the bread that is in the basket at the entrance of the tent of meeting.

verses.rationale: Preserves atonement-linked meal and holy-food restriction; outsider means outside authorized priestly group, not necessarily foreign nationality.
verses.before: They will eat those things by which atonement was made to fill their hands and consecrate them, but an outsider will not eat them, because they are holy.
verses.after: They are to eat what was used to make atonement for their ordination and consecration. No outsider may eat it, because these things are holy.
verses.tsw_comparator: They shall eat those things by which atonement was made to fill their hands and consecrate them, but an outsider shall not eat them, because they are holy.

verses.rationale: Keeps both foods, morning deadline and holiness as rationale for disposal rather than sanitation explanation.
verses.before: If any of the flesh of the ordination offering or any of the bread remains until morning, you will burn the remainder with fire. It will not be eaten, because it is holy.
verses.after: If any ordination meat or bread remains until morning, burn what is left. It must not be eaten, because it is holy.
verses.tsw_comparator: If any of the flesh of the ordination offering or any of the bread remains until morning, you shall burn the remainder with fire. It shall not be eaten, because it is holy.

verses.rationale: Preserves complete compliance and seven-day installation duration.
verses.before: “Thus you will do to Aaron and his sons according to all that I have commanded you. Seven days you will fill their hands.
verses.after: Do all this for Aaron and his sons, just as I commanded you. Their ordination is to continue for seven days.
verses.tsw_comparator: “Thus you shall do to Aaron and his sons according to all that I have commanded you. Seven days you shall fill their hands.

verses.rationale: Keeps daily bull, altar purification and anointing; does not assign moral wrongdoing to an inanimate altar.
verses.before: Each day you will offer a bull as a sin offering for atonement. You will purify the altar when you make atonement for it, and you will anoint it to consecrate it.
verses.after: Each day offer a bull as a sin offering for atonement. Purify the altar by making atonement for it, and anoint it to consecrate it.
verses.tsw_comparator: Each day you shall offer a bull as a sin offering for atonement. You shall purify the altar when you make atonement for it, and you shall anoint it to consecrate it.

verses.rationale: Keeps seven days and contact holiness as result with must-be-holy alternative noted, not a vague cleanliness rule.
verses.before: Seven days you will make atonement for the altar and consecrate it. Then the altar will be most holy; whatever touches the altar will become holy.
verses.after: For seven days make atonement for the altar and consecrate it. Then the altar will be most holy; whatever touches it will become holy.
verses.tsw_comparator: Seven days you shall make atonement for the altar and consecrate it. Then the altar shall be most holy; whatever touches the altar shall become holy.

verses.rationale: Preserves regularity, daily two and one-year age before morning/evening allocation.
verses.before: “And this is what you will offer upon the altar: two year-old lambs each day, continually.
verses.after: This is what you are to offer on the altar regularly: two lambs a year old each day.
verses.tsw_comparator: “And this is what you shall offer upon the altar: two year-old lambs each day, continually.

verses.rationale: Keeps two daily occasions and traditional twilight rendering of between-the-evenings idiom.
verses.before: The one lamb you will offer in the morning, and the second lamb you will offer at twilight.
verses.after: Offer one lamb in the morning and the other at twilight.
verses.tsw_comparator: The one lamb you shall offer in the morning, and the second lamb you shall offer at twilight.

verses.rationale: Keeps tenth flour and quarter oil/wine ratios, ancient units, and first-lamb association; ephah supplied for customary tenth measure.
verses.before: With the first lamb will be a tenth of an ephah of fine flour mixed with a quarter hin of beaten oil and a quarter hin of wine as a drink offering.
verses.after: With the first lamb, offer a tenth of an ephah of fine flour mixed with a quarter of a hin of beaten oil, and a drink offering of a quarter of a hin of wine.
verses.tsw_comparator: With the first lamb shall be a tenth of an ephah of fine flour mixed with a quarter hin of beaten oil and a quarter hin of wine as a drink offering.

verses.rationale: Preserves matching evening offerings, both categories and aroma/fire formula.
verses.before: The second lamb you will offer at twilight. You will offer with it a grain offering and drink offering like those of the morning, as a pleasing aroma, an offering by fire to the LORD.
verses.after: Offer the second lamb at twilight, with the same grain offering and drink offering as in the morning, as a pleasing aroma, an offering by fire to the LORD.
verses.tsw_comparator: The second lamb you shall offer at twilight. You shall offer with it a grain offering and drink offering like those of the morning, as a pleasing aroma, an offering by fire to the LORD.

verses.rationale: Makes Hebrew plural meeting and singular speech addressee explicit while retaining enduring recurring offering and location.
verses.before: It will be a continual burnt offering throughout your generations at the entrance of the tent of meeting before the LORD, where I will meet with you to speak to you there.
verses.after: This is to be a regular burnt offering throughout your generations, at the entrance of the tent of meeting before the LORD. There I will meet with you all and speak with you, Moses.
verses.tsw_comparator: It shall be a continual burnt offering throughout your generations at the entrance of the tent of meeting before the LORD, where I will meet with you to speak to you there.

verses.rationale: Supplies place as understood subject of consecrated while retaining divine glory as sanctifying agent; subject openness noted.
verses.before: “There I will meet with the children of Israel, and the place will be consecrated by my glory.
verses.after: I will meet with the Israelites there, and the place will be consecrated by my glory.
verses.tsw_comparator: “There I will meet with the children of Israel, and the place will be consecrated by my glory.

verses.rationale: Keeps both sacred objects and named people as recipients of divine consecration with priestly purpose.
verses.before: I will consecrate the tent of meeting and the altar. Aaron and his sons I will consecrate to serve as priests to me.
verses.after: I will consecrate the tent of meeting and the altar. I will also consecrate Aaron and his sons to serve me as priests.
verses.tsw_comparator: I will consecrate the tent of meeting and the altar. Aaron and his sons I will consecrate to serve as priests to me.

verses.rationale: Retains dwelling among people and covenantal God relationship in concise paired clauses.
verses.before: I will dwell among the children of Israel and will be their God.
verses.after: I will dwell among the Israelites and be their God.
verses.tsw_comparator: I will dwell in the midst of the children of Israel and will be their God.

verses.rationale: Preserves knowing, liberation’s dwelling purpose and repeated divine self-identification without deleting the refrain.
verses.before: They will know that I am the LORD their God, who brought them out from the land of Egypt so that I might dwell in their midst. I am the LORD their God.
verses.after: They will know that I am the LORD their God, who brought them out of Egypt to dwell among them. I am the LORD their God.”
verses.tsw_comparator: They will know that I am the LORD their God, who brought them out from the land of Egypt so that I might dwell in their midst. I am the LORD their God.

verses.rationale: Keeps incense purpose and acacia material, distinguishing this altar from the large bronze altar.
verses.before: “You will make an altar for burning incense. You will make it of acacia wood.
verses.after: “Make an altar for burning incense, using acacia wood.
verses.tsw_comparator: “You shall make an altar for burning incense. You shall make it of acacia wood.

verses.rationale: Preserves 1-by-1-by-2 dimensions, square shape and integral horns.
verses.before: It will be one cubit long and one cubit wide; it will be square, and two cubits high. Its horns will be of one piece with it.
verses.after: It is to be a cubit long and a cubit wide, forming a square, and two cubits high. Its horns must be of one piece with it.
verses.tsw_comparator: It shall be one cubit long and one cubit wide; it shall be square, and two cubits high. Its horns shall be of one piece with it.

verses.rationale: Keeps three overlay surfaces and surrounding molding, not merely a gilded top.
verses.before: You will overlay it with pure gold—its top, its sides all around, and its horns—and make a gold molding around it.
verses.after: Overlay its top, all its sides, and its horns with pure gold. Make a gold molding all around it.
verses.tsw_comparator: You shall overlay it with pure gold—its top, its sides all around, and its horns—and make a gold molding around it.

verses.rationale: Retains total two rings and opposite sides, rendering repeated side terms without multiplying them into four rings.
verses.before: You will make two gold rings for it below its molding, on two opposite sides. They will be holders for poles with which to carry it.
verses.after: Make two gold rings beneath the molding, on its two opposite sides, to hold the poles used to carry it.
verses.tsw_comparator: You shall make two gold rings for it below its molding, on two opposite sides. They shall be holders for poles with which to carry it.

verses.rationale: Keeps wood and overlay consistent with incense altar rather than bronze altar poles.
verses.before: You will make the poles of acacia wood and overlay them with gold.
verses.after: Make the poles of acacia wood and overlay them with gold.
verses.tsw_comparator: You shall make the poles of acacia wood and overlay them with gold.

verses.rationale: Preserves altar outside inner curtain, relation to testimony/cover and divine meeting promise.
verses.before: You will place it before the veil that is by the ark of the testimony, before the cover that is over the testimony, where I will meet with you.
verses.after: Put it in front of the curtain that is before the ark of the testimony, facing the atonement cover over the testimony, where I will meet with you.
verses.tsw_comparator: You shall place it before the veil that is by the ark of the testimony, before the cover that is over the testimony, where I will meet with you.

verses.rationale: Keeps Aaron as agent and repeated-morning regularity tied to lamp care.
verses.before: Aaron will burn fragrant incense on it; morning by morning, when he tends the lamps, he will burn it.
verses.after: Aaron is to burn fragrant incense on it every morning when he tends the lamps.
verses.tsw_comparator: Aaron shall burn fragrant incense on it; morning by morning, when he tends the lamps, he shall burn it.

verses.rationale: Preserves evening counterpart, lighting action, regularity and enduring generations.
verses.before: When Aaron sets up the lamps at twilight, he will burn it, a continual incense before the LORD throughout your generations.
verses.after: He is also to burn it when he lights the lamps at twilight—a regular incense offering before the LORD throughout your generations.
verses.tsw_comparator: When Aaron sets up the lamps at twilight, he shall burn it, a continual incense before the LORD throughout your generations.

verses.rationale: Keeps four prohibited categories and renders strange incense as unauthorized in sacred-use context.
verses.before: You will not offer strange incense upon it, or burnt offering or grain offering, and you will not pour a drink offering upon it.
verses.after: Do not offer unauthorized incense, a burnt offering, or a grain offering on it, and do not pour a drink offering on it.
verses.tsw_comparator: You shall not offer strange incense upon it, or burnt offering or grain offering, and you shall not pour a drink offering upon it.

verses.rationale: Preserves repeated annual interval, horn blood, offering type and intensified holiness, without importing later ritual details.
verses.before: Aaron will make atonement on its horns once a year. With the blood of the sin offering of atonement he will make atonement for it once a year throughout your generations. It is most holy to the LORD.”
verses.after: Once a year Aaron is to make atonement on its horns with blood from the sin offering for atonement. Once a year he is to make atonement for it throughout your generations. It is most holy to the LORD.”
verses.tsw_comparator: Aaron shall make atonement on its horns once a year. With the blood of the sin offering of atonement he shall make atonement for it once a year throughout your generations. It is most holy to the LORD.”

verses.rationale: Retains separate speech introduction before census instructions.
verses.before: The LORD spoke to Moses, saying,
verses.after: The LORD spoke to Moses:
verses.tsw_comparator: The LORD spoke to Moses, saying,

verses.rationale: Keeps individual male census obligation, life ransom and plague prevention; count repetition retained with full annotation hash.
verses.before: “When you take a census of the children of Israel according to people who are counted, each will give a ransom for his life to the LORD when they are counted, so that there will be no plague among them when they are counted.
verses.after: “When you take a census of the Israelites, each man must give the LORD a ransom for his life when he is counted, so that no plague strikes them during the count.
verses.tsw_comparator: “When you take a census of the children of Israel according to those who are counted, each shall give a ransom for his life to the LORD when they are counted, so that there will be no plague among them when they are counted.

verses.rationale: Preserves repeated half-shekel payment, sanctuary weight and exact twenty-gerah equivalence.
verses.before: This is what everyone who passes over to people who are counted will give: half a shekel according to the sanctuary shekel—the shekel is twenty gerahs—half a shekel as a contribution to the LORD.
verses.after: Everyone passing into the count must give half a shekel by the sanctuary standard—the shekel is twenty gerahs—half a shekel as a contribution to the LORD.
verses.tsw_comparator: This is what everyone who passes over to those who are counted shall give: half a shekel according to the sanctuary shekel—the shekel is twenty gerahs—half a shekel as a contribution to the LORD.

verses.rationale: Keeps twenty-year threshold and inclusion of all above it, not just an unstated military subgroup.
verses.before: Everyone who passes over to people who are counted, from twenty years old and upward, will give the contribution to the LORD.
verses.after: Everyone counted who is twenty years old or older must give the LORD’s contribution.
verses.tsw_comparator: Everyone who passes over to those who are counted, from twenty years old and upward, shall give the contribution to the LORD.

verses.rationale: Retains fixed equal amount and atonement rationale without turning it into a general taxation principle.
verses.before: The rich will not give more, and the poor will not give less than half a shekel when you give the contribution to the LORD to make atonement for your lives.
verses.after: The rich must not give more than half a shekel, and the poor must not give less, when you give the LORD’s contribution to make atonement for your lives.
verses.tsw_comparator: The rich shall not give more, and the poor shall not give less than half a shekel when you give the contribution to the LORD to make atonement for your lives.

verses.rationale: Keeps purpose of money, memorial link to earlier name-bearing and atonement for lives.
verses.before: You will take the atonement silver from the children of Israel and give it for the service of the tent of meeting. It will be for the children of Israel as a remembrance before the LORD, to make atonement for your lives.”
verses.after: Receive the atonement money from the Israelites and use it for the service of the tent of meeting. It will be a memorial for the Israelites before the LORD, to make atonement for your lives.”
verses.tsw_comparator: You shall take the atonement silver from the children of Israel and give it for the service of the tent of meeting. It shall be for the children of Israel as a remembrance before the LORD, to make atonement for your lives.”

verses.rationale: Preserves new speech unit introducing washing basin.
verses.before: The LORD spoke to Moses, saying,
verses.after: The LORD spoke to Moses:
verses.tsw_comparator: The LORD spoke to Moses, saying,

verses.rationale: Keeps bronze basin and stand, between-location and water requirement without inventing dimensions.
verses.before: “You will make a bronze basin with a bronze stand for washing. You will put it between the tent of meeting and the altar and put water in it.
verses.after: “Make a bronze basin with a bronze stand for washing. Put it between the tent of meeting and the altar, and fill it with water.
verses.tsw_comparator: “You shall make a bronze basin with a bronze stand for washing. You shall put it between the tent of meeting and the altar and put water in it.

verses.rationale: Preserves named male priests and both body parts rather than generic bathing.
verses.before: Aaron and his sons will wash their hands and their feet from it.
verses.after: Aaron and his sons are to wash their hands and feet with water from it.
verses.tsw_comparator: Aaron and his sons shall wash their hands and their feet from it.

verses.rationale: Makes repeated washing applicable to both entry and altar service; preserves death warning and offering purpose.
verses.before: When they enter the tent of meeting, they will wash with water so that they do not die. Or when they approach the altar to minister, to burn an offering by fire to the LORD,
verses.after: When they enter the tent of meeting, they must wash with water so they do not die. They must also wash when they approach the altar to serve by burning an offering by fire to the LORD.
verses.tsw_comparator: When they enter the tent of meeting, they shall wash with water so that they do not die. Or when they approach the altar to minister, to burn an offering by fire to the LORD,

verses.rationale: Keeps repeated washing/body parts/death and hereditary duration without collapsing the warning.
verses.before: they will wash their hands and feet so that they do not die. It will be a perpetual statute for them, for him and his offspring throughout their generations.”
verses.after: They must wash their hands and feet so they do not die. This is a lasting ordinance for Aaron and his descendants throughout their generations.”
verses.tsw_comparator: they shall wash their hands and feet so that they do not die. It shall be a perpetual statute for them, for him and his offspring throughout their generations.”

verses.rationale: Retains speech boundary before anointing-oil composition.
verses.before: The LORD spoke to Moses, saying,
verses.after: The LORD spoke to Moses:
verses.tsw_comparator: The LORD spoke to Moses, saying,

verses.rationale: Keeps five-hundred/half/two-fifty relations and generic fragrant cane rather than an uncertain specific plant identification.
verses.before: “Take for yourself the finest spices: five hundred shekels of flowing myrrh, half as much—two hundred fifty—of fragrant cinnamon, two hundred fifty of fragrant cane,
verses.after: “Take the finest spices: five hundred shekels of flowing myrrh, half that amount—two hundred fifty—of fragrant cinnamon, and two hundred fifty of fragrant cane,
verses.tsw_comparator: “Take for yourself the finest spices: five hundred shekels of flowing myrrh, half as much—two hundred fifty—of fragrant cinnamon, two hundred fifty of fragrant cane,

verses.rationale: Preserves fourth spice’s five hundred, common weight standard and one hin of oil as different measure.
verses.before: five hundred of cassia, according to the sanctuary shekel, and a hin of olive oil.
verses.after: five hundred of cassia, all by the sanctuary shekel, and a hin of olive oil.
verses.tsw_comparator: five hundred of cassia, according to the sanctuary shekel, and a hin of olive oil.

verses.rationale: Preserves skilled preparation and repeated designation without adding manufacture steps.
verses.before: You will make from these a holy anointing oil, a fragrant mixture, the work of a perfumer. It will be a holy anointing oil.
verses.after: Blend them into holy anointing oil, a perfumer’s mixture. It is to be holy anointing oil.
verses.tsw_comparator: You shall make from these a holy anointing oil, a fragrant mixture, the work of a perfumer. It shall be a holy anointing oil.

verses.rationale: Keeps oil as instrument and begins full sanctuary-object sequence.
verses.before: With it you will anoint the tent of meeting and the ark of the testimony,
verses.after: Use it to anoint the tent of meeting and the ark of the testimony,
verses.tsw_comparator: With it you shall anoint the tent of meeting and the ark of the testimony,

verses.rationale: Retains each furniture item and utensil groups, continuing the uncompressed list.
verses.before: the table and all its utensils, the lampstand and its utensils, the altar of incense,
verses.after: the table and all its utensils, the lampstand and its utensils, the incense altar,
verses.tsw_comparator: the table and all its utensils, the lampstand and its utensils, the altar of incense,

verses.rationale: Keeps second altar distinct, its utensils and both basin parts.
verses.before: the altar of burnt offering and all its utensils, and the basin and its stand.
verses.after: the altar of burnt offering and all its utensils, and the basin with its stand.
verses.tsw_comparator: the altar of burnt offering and all its utensils, and the basin and its stand.

verses.rationale: Keeps intensified holiness and contact result aligned with 29:37, with alternative prerequisite reading noted.
verses.before: You will consecrate them, and they will be most holy. Whatever touches them will become holy.
verses.after: Consecrate them so they become most holy. Whatever touches them will become holy.
verses.tsw_comparator: You shall consecrate them, and they shall be most holy. Whatever touches them shall become holy.

verses.rationale: Keeps named people separate from objects, both actions and priestly purpose.
verses.before: You will anoint Aaron and his sons and consecrate them to serve as priests to me.
verses.after: Anoint Aaron and his sons and consecrate them to serve me as priests.
verses.tsw_comparator: You shall anoint Aaron and his sons and consecrate them to serve as priests to me.

verses.rationale: Preserves nested instruction to Israel and enduring divine ownership of oil.
verses.before: You will speak to the children of Israel, saying, ‘This will be my holy anointing oil throughout your generations.
verses.after: Tell the Israelites, ‘This is to be my holy anointing oil throughout your generations.
verses.tsw_comparator: You shall speak to the children of Israel, saying, ‘This shall be my holy anointing oil throughout your generations.

verses.rationale: Retains broad bodily-use prohibition alongside commanded priestly anointing, explains restricted-use context in note without deleting tension.
verses.before: It will not be poured on ordinary human flesh, and you will not make any like it according to its composition. It is holy; it will be holy to you.
verses.after: Do not pour it on human flesh, and do not make another mixture with the same proportions. It is holy; you must treat it as holy.
verses.tsw_comparator: It shall not be poured on ordinary human flesh, and you shall not make any like it according to its composition. It is holy; it shall be holy to you.

verses.rationale: Keeps two offenses, outsider restriction and severe cut-off formula without equating it automatically with a specified mode of execution.
verses.before: Whoever mixes anything like it or whoever puts any of it on an outsider will be cut off from his people.’”
verses.after: Anyone who makes a mixture like it or applies any of it to an outsider will be cut off from their people.’”
verses.tsw_comparator: Whoever mixes anything like it or whoever puts any of it on an outsider shall be cut off from his people.’”

verses.rationale: Preserves four named aromatic substances, purity and equality; traditional ingredient identifications qualified in note.
verses.before: The LORD said to Moses, “Take fragrant spices: stacte, onycha, galbanum, and fragrant spices with pure frankincense, equal parts of each.
verses.after: The LORD said to Moses, “Take fragrant ingredients: stacte, onycha, and galbanum, along with pure frankincense, in equal quantities.
verses.tsw_comparator: The LORD said to Moses, “Take fragrant spices: stacte, onycha, galbanum, and fragrant spices with pure frankincense, equal parts of each.

verses.rationale: Chooses salted for memullah while noting alternative blended interpretation; keeps purity and holiness separate.
verses.before: Make from them incense, a fragrant mixture, the work of a perfumer, salted, pure, and holy.
verses.after: Blend them into incense, the work of a perfumer, seasoned with salt, pure and holy.
verses.tsw_comparator: Make from them incense, a fragrant mixture, the work of a perfumer, salted, pure, and holy.

verses.rationale: Keeps partial quantity ground finely, placement, meeting promise and intensified holiness.
verses.before: You will beat some of it very fine and put some of it before the testimony in the tent of meeting, where I will meet with you. It will be most holy to you.
verses.after: Grind some of it very fine and put it before the testimony in the tent of meeting, where I will meet with you. It is to be most holy to you.
verses.tsw_comparator: You shall beat some of it very fine and put some of it before the testimony in the tent of meeting, where I will meet with you. It shall be most holy to you.

verses.rationale: Preserves personal-use prohibition and divine dedication rather than banning all perfume.
verses.before: The incense that you make according to its composition you will not make for yourselves. It will be holy to you for the LORD.
verses.after: Do not make incense in these proportions for yourselves. You must treat it as holy to the LORD.
verses.tsw_comparator: The incense that you make according to its composition you shall not make for yourselves. It shall be holy to you for the LORD.

verses.rationale: Keeps intent to smell/enjoy specific mixture and cut-off sanction rather than all smelling of sanctuary incense.
verses.before: Whoever makes any like it to smell it will be cut off from his people.”
verses.after: Anyone who makes incense like it to enjoy its fragrance will be cut off from their people.”
verses.tsw_comparator: Whoever makes any like it to smell it shall be cut off from his people.”

verses.rationale: Retains separate speech introducing named artisans.
verses.before: The LORD spoke to Moses, saying,
verses.after: The LORD spoke to Moses:
verses.tsw_comparator: The LORD spoke to Moses, saying,

verses.rationale: Keeps named calling, two generations and Judah affiliation.
verses.before: “See, I have called by name Bezalel son of Uri, son of Hur, from the tribe of Judah.
verses.after: “Look, I have called Bezalel by name, the son of Uri, the son of Hur, from the tribe of Judah.
verses.tsw_comparator: “See, I have called by name Bezalel son of Uri, son of Hur, from the tribe of Judah.

verses.rationale: Retains explicit divine Spirit and all four endowments, connecting wisdom to material craftsmanship without doctrinal expansion.
verses.before: I have filled him with the Spirit of God, with wisdom, understanding, knowledge, and every kind of craftsmanship,
verses.after: I have filled him with the Spirit of God, with wisdom, understanding, knowledge, and skill in every kind of craft,
verses.tsw_comparator: I have filled him with the Spirit of God, with wisdom, understanding, knowledge, and every kind of craftsmanship,

verses.rationale: Keeps design intelligence and all three metals as purpose of endowment.
verses.before: to devise skilled designs, to work in gold, silver, and bronze,
verses.after: to devise designs and work in gold, silver, and bronze,
verses.tsw_comparator: to devise skilled designs, to work in gold, silver, and bronze,

verses.rationale: Preserves stone-setting, woodworking and comprehensive skill closing the sentence.
verses.before: in cutting stones for setting, in carving wood, and in working in every kind of craftsmanship.
verses.after: to cut stones for settings, to carve wood, and to work in every kind of craft.
verses.tsw_comparator: in cutting stones for setting, in carving wood, and in working in every kind of craftsmanship.

verses.rationale: Keeps second named artisan, father and tribe, collaboration and wider gifted workers as agents of the coming list.
verses.before: And look, I have appointed with him Oholiab son of Ahisamach, from the tribe of Dan. In the heart of everyone who are wise of heart I have put wisdom, so that they may make all that I have commanded you:
verses.after: I have appointed Oholiab son of Ahisamach, from the tribe of Dan, to work with him. I have given wisdom to every skilled worker, so they can make everything I commanded you:
verses.tsw_comparator: And look, I have appointed with him Oholiab son of Ahisamach, from the tribe of Dan. In the heart of all who are wise of heart I have put wisdom, so that they may make all that I have commanded you:

verses.rationale: Preserves tent, ark purpose, cover-on-ark and comprehensive furnishing group.
verses.before: the tent of meeting, the ark of the testimony, the cover that is upon it, and all the furnishings of the tent;
verses.after: the tent of meeting, the ark for the testimony, the atonement cover on it, and all the tent’s furnishings;
verses.tsw_comparator: the tent of meeting, the ark of the testimony, the cover that is upon it, and all the furnishings of the tent;

verses.rationale: Retains pure designation without substituting an unstated adjective, and distinguishes each utensil group and altar.
verses.before: the table and its utensils, the pure lampstand and all its utensils, the altar of incense,
verses.after: the table and its utensils, the pure lampstand and all its utensils, and the incense altar;
verses.tsw_comparator: the table and its utensils, the pure lampstand and all its utensils, the altar of incense,

verses.rationale: Keeps second altar, all utensils and both washing-basin components.
verses.before: the altar of burnt offering and all its utensils, the basin and its stand,
verses.after: the altar of burnt offering and all its utensils, and the basin with its stand;
verses.tsw_comparator: the altar of burnt offering and all its utensils, the basin and its stand,

verses.rationale: Keeps uncertain serad garments as service category with alternatives noted and retains Aaron/sons distinction.
verses.before: the woven garments, the holy garments for Aaron the priest and the garments of his sons for priestly service,
verses.after: the garments for service, the holy garments for Aaron the priest, and the garments for his sons to serve as priests;
verses.tsw_comparator: the woven garments, the holy garments for Aaron the priest and the garments of his sons for priestly service,

verses.rationale: Completes exhaustive list with oil/incense and repeated compliance command.
verses.before: the anointing oil and the fragrant incense for the Holy Place. According to all that I have commanded you, they will do.”
verses.after: the anointing oil and the fragrant incense for the sanctuary. They must make everything just as I commanded you.”
verses.tsw_comparator: the anointing oil and the fragrant incense for the Holy Place. According to all that I have commanded you, they shall do.”

verses.rationale: Preserves fresh speech boundary before Sabbath instruction.
verses.before: The LORD spoke to Moses, saying,
verses.after: The LORD said to Moses:
verses.tsw_comparator: The LORD spoke to Moses, saying,

verses.rationale: Keeps plural Sabbaths, relational sign, generational duration and knowing God as sanctifier.
verses.before: “And you, speak to the children of Israel, saying, ‘Surely you will keep my Sabbaths, for it is a sign between me and you throughout your generations, so that you may know that I am the LORD who consecrates you.
verses.after: “Tell the Israelites, ‘You must keep my Sabbaths. This is a sign between me and you throughout your generations, so you may know that I am the LORD who consecrates you.
verses.tsw_comparator: “And you, speak to the children of Israel, saying, ‘Surely you shall keep my Sabbaths, for it is a sign between me and you throughout your generations, so that you may know that I am the LORD who consecrates you.

verses.rationale: Preserves death and cut-off sanctions as separately stated, not softened to exclusion alone.
verses.before: You will keep the Sabbath, for it is holy to you. Whoever profanes it will surely be put to death. For whoever does work on it, that life will be cut off from the midst of his people.
verses.after: Keep the Sabbath, because it is holy to you. Anyone who profanes it must be put to death. Anyone who does work on it will be cut off from among their people.
verses.tsw_comparator: You shall keep the Sabbath, for it is holy to you. Whoever profanes it shall surely be put to death. For whoever does work on it, that life shall be cut off from the midst of his people.

verses.rationale: Keeps six/seventh contrast, intensive rest and repeated death penalty.
verses.before: Six days work will be done, but on the seventh day is a Sabbath of complete rest, holy to the LORD. Whoever does work on the Sabbath day will surely be put to death.
verses.after: Work may be done for six days, but the seventh day is a Sabbath of complete rest, holy to the LORD. Anyone who works on the Sabbath day must be put to death.
verses.tsw_comparator: Six days work shall be done, but on the seventh day is a Sabbath of complete rest, holy to the LORD. Whoever does work on the Sabbath day shall surely be put to death.

verses.rationale: Preserves repeated keeping/observing, covenant term and generations.
verses.before: The children of Israel will keep the Sabbath, observing the Sabbath throughout their generations as an everlasting covenant.
verses.after: The Israelites are to keep the Sabbath, observing it throughout their generations as a lasting covenant.
verses.tsw_comparator: The children of Israel shall keep the Sabbath, observing the Sabbath throughout their generations as an everlasting covenant.

verses.rationale: Retains creation rationale and vivid divine refreshment using same breathing idiom as 23:12, without erasing anthropomorphic image.
verses.before: It is a sign forever between me and the children of Israel, for in six days the LORD made the heavens and the earth, and on the seventh day he ceased and was refreshed.’”
verses.after: It is a lasting sign between me and the Israelites, because the LORD made the heavens and the earth in six days, and on the seventh day he stopped and caught his breath.’”
verses.tsw_comparator: It is a sign forever between me and the children of Israel, for in six days the LORD made the heavens and the earth, and on the seventh day he ceased and was refreshed.’”

verses.rationale: Preserves end of speech, two stone tablets, testimony term and divine finger rather than abstract authorship alone.
verses.before: When he finished speaking with Moses on Mount Sinai, he gave him the two tablets of the testimony, tablets of stone, written with the finger of God.
verses.after: When he finished speaking with Moses on Mount Sinai, he gave him the two tablets of the testimony, stone tablets written with the finger of God.
verses.tsw_comparator: When he finished speaking with Moses on Mount Sinai, he gave him the two tablets of the testimony, tablets of stone, written with the finger of God.
